events.name: Inauguration of ACE & Guest Lecture on Cyber Forensics
events.description: ACE kicked off the 2022-23 academic year with its inaugural ceremony, featuring badge distribution to club members, a recap of the previous year's activities, and introduction of the new ACE Core, Design and Web teams. Chief guest Mr. Jothi Gouthaman, Director - Cloud Reliability Engineering at Accenture, then delivered a guest lecture on Cyber Forensics covering the current cyber security landscape and prevalence of cybercrime. The event closed with a cyber-themed rapid-fire picture-word game called 'Connections' and a memento presentation to the chief guest by HOD Dr. R. Anitha.

events.name: Workshop on Data Science
events.description: ACE organised a one-day workshop on Data Science in association with Guvi Geek Networks, IITM Research Park, Chennai. HOD Dr. R. Anitha addressed the gathering on the multidisciplinary nature of data science combining mathematics, statistics, AI and computer engineering. The workshop, attended by second and third year students, covered an introduction to data science, Python basics, data analysis and visualization, and classification techniques across two sessions.
events.participants: Attended by third year and second year students

events.name: Hackerrupt'22
events.venue: Guvi Geek Network Pvt. Ltd., IITM Research Park, Chennai
events.description: Hackerrupt'22 was ACE's flagship 24-hour hackathon, run through a dedicated registration website built by the ACE team. Teams pitched and built solutions to problem statements with one-on-one mentoring from industry professionals, followed by two rounds of judging by industry experts and a final pitch by the top 5 teams. Participants praised the mentoring and judging process, and winners received goodie bags along with their placements.
events.participants: A total of 52 teams from various Engineering colleges registered, of which about 15-16 were shortlisted; the event saw a total of 57 participants, with 9 teams from SVCE and 6 from other colleges (figures as printed, slightly inconsistent in the source)

winners.name: Babycorns
winners.detail: Sathyabama Institute of Technology and Park Institute of Technology

events.prizes: 1st Place: Rs. 12,000 (visible on prize cheque in event photo)

events.name: Ace Your Potential and Code Bingo
events.venue: Respective Classrooms (Ace Your Potential) and CS Lab 1 (Code Bingo Final Round)
events.description: A two-part event for freshers: 'Ace Your Potential' was an interactive session where ACE seniors shared their experiences on placements and higher studies, followed by a preliminary round where the top two teams from each class advanced. The advancing teams then competed in 'Code Bingo' on 17th February, a code-deciphering competition, with coordinator Mr. K. Srinivasan announcing results and awarding winners. Feedback from students was very positive.

events.name: Womania
events.description: Womania was a women-only coding competition where participants could compete individually or in teams of two. An online preliminary round was conducted on the QUIZZ platform, from which 10 teams were selected to advance. In the offline final round, competitors had one hour and thirty minutes to solve five questions of varying difficulty, after which coordinator Mr. K. Srinivasan announced results and awarded prizes.
events.participants: 10 teams selected from the online prelims to the final round
events.requirements: Participants could enter as a team of 2 or individually; prelims held online, finals held offline with 5 questions of varying difficulty to be solved in 1 hour 30 minutes

events.name: Interrupt'23
events.description: Interrupt'23 was ACE's National Level Technical Symposium, inaugurated on 31st March 2023 with chief guest Mr. Damodharan J, Member Leadership Staff at Zoho Corporation, Chennai, who delivered a motivational address encouraging students to pursue their goals. The symposium comprised nine distinct technical and non-technical events (Joker Coder, Darwin Charles, Glitch Hunters, Present At The Moment, Debate-ch, Code Relay, Crack The Lock, Webworx, and Paper Presentation) open to students from colleges across the state. In total, 684 participants took part across the nine events, drawing teams from colleges including Saveetha Engineering College, Rajalakshmi Engineering College, SRM Institute of Science and Technology, Sri Sairam Engineering College, RMK Engineering College, and several others.
events.participants: Total number of participants: 684; Total number of events: 9

events.name: Joker Coder
events.description: A two-level puzzle-solving event held as part of Interrupt'23. In the first level, teams had to decrypt seven encrypted answers, and in the second level they had to solve three issues while navigating a variety of fun obstacles.
events.requirements: Level 1: decrypt seven encrypted answers. Level 2: solve three issues while navigating fun obstacles.

events.name: Darwin Charles
events.description: A reverse-engineering themed competition held as part of Interrupt'23. Ten teams were shortlisted after a first phase of aptitude and programming questions, and finalists were then given only an executable file and had to reverse engineer it in the second phase.
events.participants: Ten teams shortlisted to the final phase
events.requirements: Phase 1: aptitude and programming questions to shortlist 10 teams. Phase 2: reverse engineering of an exe file given only to finalists.

events.name: Glitch Hunters
events.description: A debugging-focused event held as part of Interrupt'23. The first round was a common MCQ filtering round, after which finalists solved a crossword, with only one team member allowed to debug at a time, swapping with a teammate every 10 minutes.

winners.name: HARSHAN T S, AJAY KUMAAR M

events.requirements: Round 1: common MCQ round for filtering. Round 2 (finalists): crossword-based debugging with only one teammate allowed to debug at a time, swapped every 10 minutes.

events.name: Present At The Moment
events.description: An event held as part of Interrupt'23 where an offline first round filtered contestants who then advanced to an offline final stage, in which they could question and challenge the work of their rivals.
events.requirements: Round 1: offline filtering round. Round 2 (finalists): offline stage where contestants may question rivals' work.

events.name: Debate-ch
events.description: A debate competition held as part of Interrupt'23. Two teams argued for and against a motion, with each member given three minutes to speak, and no points of interruption allowed during the first or last 30 seconds of a speech.
events.requirements: Two teams debate for/against a motion; each speaker gets 3 minutes; no point of interruption (POI) allowed in the first or last 30 seconds.

events.name: Code Relay
events.description: A relay-style coding event held as part of Interrupt'23 in which team members played alternately across a sequence of three rounds to complete the task.

winners.name: MOHAMMED TAHEER R, MOHITH, AAKASH G, PRAKASH R
BHAVAN ARIMAAN T, BALAJI C K, CHANAKIYA KSHATRIYA A

events.requirements: Team members play alternately to complete a sequence of three rounds.

events.name: Crack The Lock
events.description: A quiz-and-puzzle event held as part of Interrupt'23. The first round was a quiz based on the most Googled questions of the past two years, and the second round required participants to respond to a problem statement that hinted at the next question, with the final phrases together revealing the secret to opening a mysterious box.

winners.name: KEERTHANA Y, NIVETHA R
winners.detail: RMK College of Engineering, Sri Venkateswara College of Engineering

events.requirements: Round 1: quiz round on the most Googled questions of the past 2 years. Round 2: solve problem statements that hint at the next question, culminating in a secret phrase to open a box.

events.name: Webworx
events.description: A web development event held as part of Interrupt'23 that challenged participants to test their web-building abilities by constructing a replica of a vintage website, as a tribute to the early builders of the internet.
events.requirements: Participants build a replica of a vintage website.

events.name: Paper Presentation
events.description: A paper presentation competition held as part of Interrupt'23. Participants first submitted an abstract of their concept via a form on the ACE website to qualify for the final round, where full data/paper submission was required.
events.requirements: Round 1: submit an abstract of the concept via a form on the ACE website. Round 2 (finalists): full paper/data submission.
